title: Publish the outage commitment the record already supports, by Fri 4 Dec
description: There is a goal for a status page but none for commitments. Nothing states what uptime Zedu targets, what a customer can expect when it is missed, or what support response a paid plan gets. Measure first: pull ninety days of incident notes and support threads, record time to first reply and time to resolution, and report the distribution rather than the average. Then publish only the commitment the record can meet four times out of five, next to the plan it applies to.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Decide what happens when the commitment is missed, and who says so publicly
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A commitment without a consequence is marketing. The honest options are a service credit, a public explanation, or both, and each needs an owner and a trigger. Work: write the rule for each measured miss — who is notified, what the customer receives, in what window, and who signs the public message. Include the awkward case where the miss is our fault but small. Deliver the rule, the customer-facing wording, and the named role responsible for triggering it, not a team name.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Measure ninety days before promising a minute of it
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Every number on this page will be tested by the first customer who has a bad week. Work: take the last ninety days of incident notes, support threads and status entries, and record for each event the time it started, how it was noticed, time to first customer-facing update, and time to resolution. Report the distribution, not the average. Deliver the table, the four numbers the record can support, and the honest note on what the data cannot show because nobody recorded it at the time.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Set the review cadence so the promise cannot rot silently
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A published commitment becomes false the first time the team gets slower and nobody looks. Work: define the quarterly review — who runs it, which data, what triggers a change to the published number, and how a downgrade is announced rather than quietly edited. Put the measurement in the same place as the status record so the two cannot disagree. Deliver the review procedure, the first run on the existing data, and the sentence that explains to a customer why a number changed.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Write the commitment in the customer's terms rather than the infrastructure's
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Customers do not experience "database availability"; they experience not being able to sign in or a call dropping mid-session. Work: turn the measured events into commitments about moments — signing in, opening a channel, joining a live session, opening a file — each with a target and a defined start and stop. Then state what does not count. Deliver the four moments with their targets, the exclusions in plain words, and the version for the pricing page under the paid plan it applies to.
